headline: High risk of cascading errors and capability conflict; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but non-zero due to shared MCP/network surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a can use MCP and stdin/stdout, so it may ingest untrusted content; agent_b exposes integrations and broad network egress, creating a plausible bridge if outputs are copied into support workflows. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF agent_a output is pasted into agent_b ticket fields or integrations
IF either agent parses the other's text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw agent output into support workflows for one test run
Add a fixed delimiter around agent outputs before ingestion
Require human review of any instruction-like text
Turn off nonessential integrations for the session

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b handles customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and messages, while agent_a touches task prompts, code, and repository metadata and can use network egress plus MCP. A shared workspace is not documented, but if one exists, leakage from support data into agent_a's outputs or upstream services is plausible.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or ticket export
IF agent_a receives customer records or messages as input
mitigations: Keep customer records out of agent_a inputs
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
Redact messages before any handoff
Disable network egress for the test session if feasible

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b has broad network egress and integrations. If both operate on the same repo or mutable resource, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite each other's changes. The shared target is not explicit, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or directory
IF agent_b triggers actions that mutate the same external resource agent_a edits
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Serialize write operations with a lock
Disable git writes for one agent during the run
Review diffs before merge

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate code, repository metadata, and task outputs, and agent_b is a customer-support system with integrations that may act on incoming content. If agent_b treats agent_a's output as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into customer-facing actions or reports. No verification mechanism is documented, so the safer higher severity applies.
conditions: IF agent_b forwards agent_a output into customer-facing replies or automations
IF no human verification step exists between the agents
mitigations: Insert a mandatory review step before any outbound action
Mark agent_a output as untrusted metadata
Limit agent_b to drafting only, not sending
Log provenance for every handoff

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b clearly processes customer data and interaction history, while agent_a touches task prompts and repository metadata and can use network egress. The profiles do not state residency, retention, or certification boundaries, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven; uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF customer data from agent_b is routed through agent_a
IF retention or residency policies differ between the two systems
mitigations: Keep regulated customer data out of agent_a
Document data flow boundaries before deployment
Compare retention settings for both systems
Restrict exports to minimized fields
